source_correspondence: The complex-cutoff estimate is Proposition26.6.1-prime, with the measured forcing, incoming data and Hbeta input, including e=1/4. The joint inequality is CCA:CA13.

The bandwise ordinary extension has uniform first and higher normalized derivatives. The actual C1 plateau supplies shrinking sign balls. Finite-radius Taylor control yields a two-point bound even when the connecting segment leaves the sign set.

A capped infimum of cones extends the root weight to all phase space. No minimizer or differentiability is presumed. Its exact Lipschitz inequality proves local comparability; the two global reverse-ratio cases prove symplectic temperateness uniformly in frequency.

The adaptive metric satisfies uncertainty. The smaller constant exotic metric and the adaptive metric satisfy every cross condition of the actual two-metric Weyl theorem, with cross parameter EH/R. All weights are locally continuous and temperate.

All differentiated square-root estimates are proved from the ordinary Hessian bound and finite-radius gradient bound. The complete Weyl square defect has weight max(A^2 E^4/R^2,A^-2), uniformly bounded through the quarter endpoint.

The leading complex commutator has the exact weak-order bound in both root regimes, with the improved positive-derivative gain in the large-root regime. The full second remainder uses two different metrics and has strictly sufficient order; it is not inferred from a principal bracket.

The full second commutator has bounded weight A*h, and commuting through every fixed bounded error is controlled with the distinct-metric first remainder. All constants are uniform on the relevant symbol families.

The exact imaginary-part factorization includes the order-zero term and the complete square defect. The off-sign composition has every coefficient zero and an arbitrarily small full constant-metric remainder. Completing the square proves the band form bound.

The leading band constant depends on the fixed imaginary symbol and sign cutoff, not on the complex measured symbol or energy weight. Weight-dependent constants multiply only weak input terms, split using fixed Young coefficients.

The dyadic IMS identity has its exact sign and full summed remainder. Both commutators with ordinary frequency cutoffs have their sharper mixed losses. Retained coefficients have bounded overlap; separated-frequency Fourier kernel bounds and Schur estimates control all tail remainders.

Finite band quantization errors preserve the exact plateau support, cover every real s and require only the explicit loss N*kappa>=2-3e. The band estimates and norm localization sum with precisely the Hbeta norm.

The actual left-regularized operator is restored by a complete finite symbol expansion and a proved lower-order perturbation estimate. This step never substitutes a stronger forcing measurement. The leading constant stays independent of Lambda and nu.

The existing full energy identity, outgoing two-order defect, left data contractions and distributional weak limit apply to the complex symbol. The proved joint bound closes their absorption with Lambda chosen only after K.
